title: Madonna Enthroned with the Child, Saint Francis and Four Angels

museum.name: Lower Basilica of San Francesco, Assisi

source.label: Crowe and Cavalcaselle: “In the Lower Church … Cimabue probably adorned the right transept”
Wikipedia: “in the transept of the Lower Basilica of San Francesco, he created a fresco”

work.text: Surrounded by the works of Giotto, on the right hand of that part of the building, is one of an earlier date … a colossal Virgin and Child between four angels.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 2 (ed. Langton Douglas)

work.text: Placed above the altar of the Conception, and much damaged by restoring, it reveals the manner of Cimabue.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 2 (ed. Langton Douglas)

moment.text: At Assisi, in the transept of the Lower Basilica of San Francesco, he created a fresco named Madonna with Child Enthroned, Four Angels and St Francis. The left portion of this fresco is lost, but it may have shown St Anthony of Padua (the authorship of the painting has been recently disputed for technical and stylistic reasons).

matters.text: During the pontificate of Pope Nicholas IV, the first Franciscan pope, … Cimabue worked in Assisi.
Francis had died in 1226, roughly two generations before this fresco, so Cimabue never saw him. The saint stands at the edge of a heavenly court, in the church built over his tomb.
